records.region: Northwestern Arizona; eastern Truxton feeder–Truxton Wash–Hualapai Valley–Red Lake playa
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the receiving Truxton Wash system, including the selected unnamed eastern feeder, the named upper and lower wash and its entry into Red Lake. The feeder is not independently assigned the Truxton name. Red Lake is a distinct terminal playa, not an alias or river scalar name.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary source correspondence for all 34 parts of the one stage-3 mainstem fragment, including chosen opening, unnamed feeder join, every intervening corridor, tributary junctions, actual southern Red Lake entry and final playa ending. No material intervening transfer gap remains.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the receiving Truxton Wash system, including the selected unnamed eastern feeder, the named upper and lower wash and its entry into Red Lake. The feeder is not independently assigned the Truxton name. Red Lake is a distinct terminal playa, not an alias or river scalar name.

scope_limits: The small eastern selected feeder remains unnamed in inspected cartography; Truxton Wash is a representative receiving-system identity rather than a scalar label for every selected position.

No exact source, bank, tributary confluence vertex, hydronym boundary, Korean rendering, formal registry status or current water/flow condition is verified.

records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The chosen feeder, fan entry, continuous receiving-floor setting and actual modeled terminal are accounted for. A river channel is not required across the saline floor, and no separate interbasin or managed transfer is indicated. The salt-flat name and an independently described southwestern Río Grande must not be assigned to this northeastern feeder.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative natural-river name is established for the selected northeastern feeder and its long continuation inside a receiving salar. Salar de Arizaro is recorded separately as the receiving salt flat, not as a river name.
records.completion_scope: An unnamed north-to-south dry feeder widens into an alluvial fan and enters the northeastern margin of a broad salar. The remaining selected continuation runs southwest and then east within the same receiving Arizaro salt-flat setting. Ordinary geographic correspondence is complete, but the inspected sources do not supply a supported whole-system river hydronym.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative natural-river name is established for the selected northeastern feeder and its long continuation inside a receiving salar. Salar de Arizaro is recorded separately as the receiving salt flat, not as a river name.

scope_limits: The northeastern feeder has no supported hydronym in the inspected sources; null means unestablished, not officially unnamed.

records.region: Panama, western Bocas del Toro; Costa Rica–Panama border-region drainage context
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative connected-system identity for the selected western Estrella/Estrellita feeder, receiving Changuinola valley, managed reservoir passage and Caribbean outlet. Distinct component names do not become aliases for the whole system.
records.completion_scope: Both mainstem FIDs, all 48 stored parts and both stages have ordinary corridor-scale correspondence, including the chosen opening, Estrella/Clarito-side transition, Estrellita–Changuinola junction, Culubre entry, reservoir/dam-side passage, lower intermediate joins, fragment join, Teribe confluence setting and actual sea ending. No selected tributary FID, glacier or additional through-lake requires coverage.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative connected-system identity for the selected western Estrella/Estrellita feeder, receiving Changuinola valley, managed reservoir passage and Caribbean outlet. Distinct component names do not become aliases for the whole system.

scope_limits: Río Changuinola is representative receiving-system identity, not a scalar name imposed on Río Estrella, Río Estrellita or the unnamed tiny opening. Exact source and name-transition vertices remain unassigned.

The 1986 ETESA schematic generalizes the western branch as Changuinola; the more detailed MiAmbiente basin map distinguishes Estrella/Estrellita. This is retained as source-dependent naming scope, not treated as an unqualified whole-system synonym.
The Río Clarito, Río Lajas, Río Ceiba, Río Culubre, Río Risco and Río Teribe labels are contextual tributary identities. No selected upstream tributary fragment is assigned their name.

The thematic basin map is undated in its printed margin and predates or omits modern reservoir depiction. Imagery and current institutional infrastructure/station descriptions supply the reservoir corridor correspondence.

Canopy obscures individual wetted threads in the western opening; the continuous mapped drainage and corresponding valley resolve the ordinary corridor without demanding exact-bank or current-flow proof.
The selected mainstem remains geographically continuous through the managed valley; discharge, gate settings, powerplant routing and current operating conditions are not established.
Formal official-name registry verification remains unperformed.

records.region: Sierra de la Giganta through the Santo Domingo plain and estuary, Loreto and Comondú municipalities, Baja California Sur, Mexico.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Santo Domingo identifies the receiving lower river and its coastal outlet. The connected selected upper and middle course includes the separately labeled Santa Cruz, Querétaro and La Peña reaches. Those component names are not whole-system aliases, and the unnamed initial feeder is not given an invented name.
records.completion_scope: Ordinary source correspondence covers the full chosen opening and all thirty stored parts, the paired municipal-map transition, foothill joins, broad southern alluvial turn, Querétaro and La Peña corridor through cultivated land, receiving Santo Domingo join, lower bends, tidal continuation and actual stored endpoint. Different reach hydronyms remain separate. The evidence supports a representative connected-system identity without assigning one scalar name to every reach.
records.supported_name_scope: Santo Domingo identifies the receiving lower river and its coastal outlet. The connected selected upper and middle course includes the separately labeled Santa Cruz, Querétaro and La Peña reaches. Those component names are not whole-system aliases, and the unnamed initial feeder is not given an invented name.

scope_limits: The short eastern opening has no independently assigned component hydronym; Santa Cruz is retained only for the labeled adjoining upper valley.
Exact boundaries between Santa Cruz, unnamed connecting reaches, Querétaro, La Peña and Santo Domingo are not assigned to model vertices.
The endpoint is inside the estuarine receiving setting, not a claim that the selection reaches the seaward side of the barrier or follows one currently active tidal branch.
Arid channels and broad alluvial fans may be dry, diffuse or distributary. The evidence establishes ordinary connected geography, not continuous present water or managed-system operation.
Mangrove-like tidal vegetation is visible, but species-level ecological classification was not independently verified.
No official registry verification, surveyed source/mouth, exact river length or product naming application is made.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
